steps.text: Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
In a small bowl, mix the olive oil, garlic, rosemary, basil, Italian seasoning, black pepper and salt. Set aside.

Wash the turkey inside and out; pat dry. Remove any large fat deposits. Loosen the skin from the breast. This is done by slowly working your fingers between the breast and the skin. Work it loose to the end of the drumstick, being careful not to tear the skin.

Using your hand, spread a generous amount of the rosemary mixture under the breast skin and down the thigh and leg. Rub the remainder of the rosemary mixture over the outside of the breast. Use toothpicks to seal skin over any exposed breast meat.

Place the turkey on a rack in a roasting pan. Add about 1/4 inch of water to the bottom of the pan. Roast in the preheated oven 3 to 4 hours, or until the internal temperature of the bird reaches 180 degrees F (80 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Rosemary Roasted Turkey
raw_recipe.description: In this method, which can be used with all types of poultry, olive oil infused with garlic and rosemary is rubbed between the skin and meat of the bird before roasting.

video.description: A moist, flavorful roast turkey rubbed with garlic and fresh herbs.

review.reviewBody: This was the best turkey i had ever made. I added fresh italian seasoning that it asked for instead of dried, such as marjoram, thyme, oregano, etc. I did not add sage since it overpowers foods and so does the rosemary so you have to choose one. When i cooked the turkey i cooked it breast side down..that is the best secret to having a moist delicous turkey..also cover with foil, if you are not stuffing the turkey throw some rosemary sprigs inside the cavity with whatever vegetables you may choose as well. The last 45 min. to an hour take the foil off and turn the turkey breast side up so it can brown.
I substituted the water with white wine. Very tasty

Excellent recipe! I also followed Trivert's suggestion, brining the turkey using their recipe for about 14 hours prior to roasting. I added garlic cloves, basil, rosemary, and peppercorns to the brine, then removed the basil, rosemary, and garlic for incorporating into the rub. I cooked the bird (minus the roasting rack since I didn't have one) in an aluminum pan with about 1/4 cup of white wine + 1/4 cup of water. It was absolutely perfect. I did not cover it with foil, cook it upside down, use toothpicks to close the exposed meat, or baste it. I used some of the drippings for perfect gravy using another Allrecipes recipe (see "Rich Turkey Gravy"; I also added about 1/4 cup white wine - another super easy recipe). In the future, this will be my go-to recipe for roasting a turkey.

I used this recipe when making my very first roast turkey. Since I had made roast chicken before, I knew I wanted to use real salted butter (Land O' Lakes) instead of olive oil (I omitted the salt in the recipe since I used salted butter), and I doubled up on all the ingredients since I wanted to make sure my turkey was moist with the butter. 

In addition to substituting butter for the olive oil and doubling up, I also tweaked the recipe in adding more garlic than called for. I also used a disposable roasting pan and did not use a roasting rack or the water that was called for. If you use enough butter, you don't need to the water to keep the turkey moist...plus, the water spoils the drippings for the gravy.

I also cooked the bird breast-down, that way the breast was cooked in the butter and spices when it melted. I still spooned the melted butter/spice mixture over the exposed portion of the bird, however, to make sure all the meat was moistened and delicious. I used the drippings to make the gravy.

The turkey and gravy turned out perfect! My husband said it was the best turkey and gravy he'd ever eaten (and his parents are fabulous cooks).

The first turkey I ever made, and hands down, it was the BEST turkey EVER! Seriously! We had about 20-25 people and my friend was asked to make one of the turkeys for her family. She had an 18lbs turkey. We weren't able to get the fresh herbs but we used this recipe as our base. We used freeze-dried poultry herb by lite house, dried basil, olive oil, salt& pepper, season salt. We used 2 cups olive oil, a whole container of the poultry herbs, 1/4 ounce of dried basil, 4 tablespoons of minced garlic, 1 tsp pepper, 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp season salt. We lightly sprinkled season salt on the whole turkey (skin). We mixed together all our ingredients and followed the instructions from there. We didn't cook the stuffing in the turkey so we seasoned the inside of the turkey too. We put the turkey in an oven baked bag and poured what was left over from the mixture in the bag. We let it marinade over night. We cooked the turkey breast down so the breast could cook in all those juices. Seriously, this turkey was murdered within minutes and everyone asked for the recipe!

My husband was supposed to deep fry a turkey for thanksgiving but he got called out of town. Allrecipes came to the rescue when I got stuck making the turkey. This recipe was perfectly simple. The turkey was nicely brown and quite moist. This will be my go to recipe every thanksgiving.

The only changes I made after reading other reviews was I used butter instead of olive oil. I covered the turkey for the first 2 hours only. Then cooked uncovered for 2 hours. I did drizzle olive oil on the turkey when I took off the cover. Also the final 2 hours I periodically rotated the turkey around in the oven to give it an even back. For next time I will leave the turkey covered for first 3 hours to see that eliminates my need to rotate the turkey. I used a 10 lb turkey. It couldn't have been any easier or moisture. I think adding water to the pan and using butter contributed to the moistness.

i have made similar turkey for the past 10 years. I make small slivers of fresh garlic (3-4 cloves) and equal amount of slivered butter. Strategically slip a sliver of the garlic & butter, together, under the skin until you use it all. put 2-3 cloves of garlic and 1 3-4" sprig of fresh rosemary in the cavity. roast the turkey. use the dripping to make the most amazing gravy ever!!

I really liked the simplicity of this recipe. I did take the advice of others and used less olive oil, about 1/2 cup for a 13 lb. fresh turkey. I did throw some onion quarters, orange quarters and thyme and sage in the cavity. I found it cooked quicker than I expected (probably because I used a Convection/Roast setting). I tented it when it started to get too brown and added water periodically. The gravy was amazing.

This was my first turkey (and I'm 52 LOL). Here's what I did that is a little different from the recipe. No, Italian seasoning. 1 T kosher salt in with mix of 1/4 olive oil and 1/4 cup butter and herb mixture. I mixed 1 T kosher salt with 1/2 T poultry seasoning for the cavity and put in some quartered onions and some extra rosemary. Cooked at 350 for 4.5 hours for my 13 pound previously frozen turkey. I mixed 1 packet of chicken broth (dissolved) into the 4 cups of boiling water. I roasted it for the first 2 hours without foil and then covered. Then I basted it twice, once after 3.5 hours and again after 4 hours. Could have done sooner I'm sure. I let it rest for 30 minutes with an extra towel over it before carving. Served with roasted carrots, cauliflower and onions and Mom's famous stuffing. Yum!

This is just the best way to make a really juicy, flavorful turkey. My only changes were to use 1/2 olive oil to 1/2 butter and to add fresh thyme, and sage with the rosemary and basil. i find that the mixture is easier to spread under the skin with the butter and the effect is delicious. This also works well with a roasted chicken.

My family LOVES this recipe. I have made my turkey this way for about 10 years. I usually double the recipe because we have 18-20 lb. turkeys. I always cover the turkey with cheese cloth soaked in chicken stock and use the stock instead of water in the bottom of the pan. Then baste the cheese cloth every 20 min. When you remove the cheese cloth it is beautiful. This year I am going to try to do the rub the day before to let the flavor marinate the meat.

This was delicious and I am not a cook's cook, if that makes any sense at all. I followed the directions and had delicious, moist turkey will a beautiful browned, herbed skin that looked beautiful when it was done!
Every year come back for this recipe!!! A family favorite!!! Thank you!!!

My second review. Still love it, but this time I didn't have fresh herbs. It was just as good with dried. I did something else different though. This Thanksgiving, I made the turkey a day early, so it would be less stress on T-day. I also made the gravy ahead of time. I still can't believe how great it came out. I can hardly wait until my guests come tomorrow! I just made a roux and added it to the liquid in the pan, and it made a perfect gravy. Okay, Here's my 2024 review! I made this turkey again this year. This time, I made it Sunday for Thursday's Thanksgiving. I got it all sliced up and it is in the freezer now, and I will take it out a day or two before the big day. Tomorrow I will make the gravy, using an easy recipe I found in The NY Times by Mark Bittman. I will attach a photo of the turkey from today. My husband had dinner from the scraps of today's slicing leftovers. One quibble; The recipe says to cook until the temp is 180 degrees, which is way too well done. I cooked until it was 165. It was perfect. I will reheat it in the oven just until it is serving temp, and the potatoes and brussels sprouts will be able to fit in the oven at the same time. With an applesauce bread in my bread maker, all the hot dishes will be taken care of. I used fresh basil that I grow indoors, and my house still smells wonderful from all those spices! I just love this recipe!
Scrumptious! My whole family ONLY wants it made this way now (3-4 years in a row now).
Absolutely the best roast turkey recipe ever. Perfect.
Have made 4 times and it gets great reviews every time.
Best turkey I've ever made. Been using this recipe for years. I do spread butter all over the turkey first. It's always soft, moist and delicious!!!
Easily the best turkey I have ever had. Thank you for this. Turned the remaining juices left over into frozen dog treats, made about 100. She thanks you too…!
I NEVER have left overs....5 or 6 years strong now!!
